summary: Iteration 1 confirmed all directional predictions: prefill-decode disaggregation (AD) consistently lowers inter-token latency (ITL) and raises time-to-first-token (TTFT) compared to always-local (AL) across all 7 arrival rates (10–130 req/s) and 3 seeds. The ITL gap widens from 0.13 ms at low load to 1.68 ms at high load, and the α/(1-ρ) formula fits both curves (R²=0.94 AL, 0.96 AD). The main open question is where the formula breaks down near saturation — rates above 130 req/s have not been tested.
key_points: ITL: AD < AL at all 21 rate×seed combinations. Mean ITL at rate=130: AL=19.45 ms vs AD=17.77 ms (gap of 1.68 ms). At rate=10 the gap is only 0.13 ms — exactly as predicted by the 1/(1-ρ) nonlinearity growing with load.
TTFT: AD > AL at all conditions by 4.2–9.4 ms, attributed to a constant ~3.4 ms KV transfer cost plus prefill-server queueing — confirms the paper's pipeline overhead mechanism.

Formula fit quality is good but not perfect: R²=0.9441 (AL) vs the 0.95 target, likely due to coarse parameter search grid rather than a true model failure; system operates in the near-linear regime (ρ < 0.5) throughout the tested range, so the dramatic knee of 1/(1-ρ) has not yet been observed.

Key surprise: In AL mode, 2 of 4 instances (the prefill servers) sit completely idle — AL effectively uses half the cluster. This means AL vs AD is not a fair resource comparison, but it does match the paper's assumed setup.

Next iteration should push arrival rates to 140–170 req/s to probe the saturation boundary and formula breakdown point, and optionally test the prefix-threshold decider as an intermediate policy between AL and AD.
